growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal, usually with 3-5 needle-like cotyledons. For about the first year the seedling wears soft, spreading needle-like juvenile leaves 4-8 mm long before switching to tiny, tight, bright green scale leaves. Young trees are dense, narrow cones branched to the ground; only with age and wind do they turn broad, flat-topped and sculpted.
growth.source: USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual, Cupressus (pollinates March; cones ripen 15-18 months after pollination; ~140 seeds/cone; cones before age 10; germination tested over 35 d, 60-90 d stratification); Wikipedia Hesperocyparis macrocarpa (juvenile needle leaves 4-8 mm; oldest verified 284 yr; few natives >100 yr)

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (seed cones globose-oblong 20-40 mm, 6-14 scales, green maturing brown 20-24 months after pollination; pollen cones 3-5 mm shed late winter-early spring); USDA WPSM (15-18 months, ~140 seeds/cone). Cone persistence, set, crop and decay estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with 5-8 cotyledons, often perched on rotting nurse logs in coastal rainforest. Saplings are open, symmetrical cones with widely spaced branch whorls and stiff, very sharp, flattened blue-green needles standing out all around the twig; side branchlets droop.
growth.source: USDA Silvics (Harris): ~27 m within 50 years of reaching breast height on average SE Alaska sites; cones occasionally before 20 yrs, in stands from 20-40; good crops every 3-8 years; tolerant of shade (less than hemlock); may live 700-800 years

fruiting.source: USDA Silvics (pollen shed late April to early June; cones ripen the year they are pollinated, seed ripe late Aug-early Sep; dispersal from October, 73% within 6 weeks); cone size 5-10 cm from floras; crop and decay estimated

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny plumed achenes land on bare mineral soil and sprout in 2-4 weeks. The seedling has two small round cotyledons, then small, glossy, bright-green, wedge-shaped leaves with a few teeth, over a deep taproot. It branches quickly from the base into a dense, rounded or sprawling mound of stiff, crowded green twigs.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Baccharis pilularis (germination mostly within 15-30 d without pretreatment, shade-intolerant, poor seedling growth in shade, individuals live 10-15 yr but basal sprouting and layering extend it); first flowering age estimated.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS (dioecious, flowers Jul-Oct, 55 insect visitor species incl. honey bees, achenes 1-2 mm with 6-10 mm pappus, ripe Sep-Nov, dispersed Oct-Jan); counts are flower heads, estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings appear only after a rare mass flowering: grass-like tufts of a few thin culms 10-20 cm tall with small leaves; each year the clump sends up taller culms from spreading rhizomes. Mature culms 1-3 m, arching at the base under snow, with big oblong leaves crowded at the top; each new culm reaches full height in about 2 months of early summer.
growth.source: Makita 1992 Ecological Research (Sasa kurilensis is monocarpic: after mass flowering the stand dies and regrows from seedlings over one to two decades); Japanese bamboo literature (culms 1-3 m, shoots May-June, edible 'nemagari-dake'); flowering interval not known, estimated as many decades

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling with small round cotyledons, then paired, round, glossy dark-green leaves with a pale midrib, as in the adult. It creeps from the start: thin stems lie flat, root at the nodes and branch, slowly knitting into a loose evergreen mat only a few cm high; paired white tubular flowers share one ovary, so each red berry shows two dimples.
growth.source: Wikipedia Mitchella repens (creeping, under 6 cm tall, stems 15-30 cm rooting and branching into loose mats; berries ripen Jul-Oct and persist over winter; shady woods); seed dormancy (needs a winter, often longer) and mat growth estimated from nursery propagation guides

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny seedlings on rotting logs and stumps (light needed to germinate): two small cotyledons, then leathery, finely toothed oval leaves. Very slow at first (only 8-13 cm after 2-3 years); then spreads by layering and rhizomes into a thicket of zigzag, reddish, glandular-hairy stems with glossy, thick, egg-shaped evergreen leaves.
growth.source: USDA FEIS species review (Gaultheria shallon): germination in 27-45 days, light required; seedlings slow, 3-5 in after 2-3 yr; flowers only at >=5 yr; twigs live 16+ yr and rhizomes for centuries; shade-tolerant but less vigorous under dense canopy.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS (flowers May-Jul, white to pink urn-shaped flowers on terminal bracteate racemes, ~6 per twig, bee and fly pollinated; hairy blue-black pseudoberries 6-10 mm ripen Aug-Oct and may persist to December, ~126 seeds each; regular good crops). Fruit set, rot and crop estimated.

epiphyte.silhouette: leafy tangle high in host trees

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two oval cotyledons, then small, glossy, round to heart-shaped leaves with coarse blunt teeth on a thin stem. The seedling trails along the forest floor for a year or more, rooting where it touches, with simple unbranched tendrils; once it reaches a trunk it climbs fast. Its bark stays tight and smooth with pale lenticels instead of shredding like other grapes.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Vitis rotundifolia): crops can start in 3-5 years; NC State Extension plant toolbox: rapid growth, full sun to part shade. Lifespan from the roughly 400-year-old Mother Vine on Roanoke Island, NC; germination and height curve estimated.

fruiting.source: NC State Extension plant toolbox (Vitis rotundifolia): small greenish-white flowers May-Jun in axillary panicles; berries 1/2-1 inch, dark purple or bronze, borne singly or in small groups, not large clusters, ripe Aug-Oct; Wikipedia: many cultivars pistillate, a few perfect-flowered. Ripe berries drop one by one; pollinators, fruit set and crop estimated.

epiphyte.silhouette: long grey curtains hanging from branches

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are minute grey tufts of thread-like leaves on bark, but most new plants start as windblown or bird-carried fragments. A young plant is a short, curly chain of silvery-grey scaly stems with 2-6 cm thread leaves, lengthening over years into festoons that hang 1-6 m (rarely 8 m) from branches, with tiny three-petalled flowers in spring.
growth.source: Wikipedia Spanish moss (leaves 2-6 cm x 1 mm; hanging festoons to 6 m, rarely 8 m; spreads by seed and by fragments carried by wind and nesting birds; small flowers with spreading petals). Seed germination, strand growth rate, first flowering and festoon age estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Spores sprout on moss and bark of oak limbs into tiny heart-shaped prothalli; the first fronds are small, simple to shallowly lobed and leathery, then once-pinnatifid fronds with grey-scaly undersides. A slender creeping rhizome (about 2 mm thick) branches along the bark into a mat. In drought the fronds curl up grey-brown and look dead, turning green again within a day or two of rain.
growth.source: Wikipedia Pleopeltis polypodioides (fronds to 25 x 5 cm; rhizome 2 mm; survives losing up to 97% of its water and rehydrates in 24-48 h; spores summer to autumn; rhizome pieces root). Spore-to-plant time, growth and lifespan estimated from epiphytic Polypodiaceae.
